turns.prompt_text: is B6 or B12 doing that's bad for you
turns.response_html:
Excessive Vitamin B6 is generally considered more dangerous because it can cause permanent nerve damage.

While both are water-soluble and usually safe, high doses of supplements carry different risks:

Vitamin B6 (Pyridoxine)

Taking too much B6 (typically over 100mg daily) can lead to peripheral neuropathy.

  • Symptoms: Tingling, burning, or numbness in the hands and feet.
  • Severity: In extreme cases, it can cause difficulty walking or loss of muscle coordination.
  • Recovery: Symptoms often improve after stopping, but some damage may be permanent.

Vitamin B12 (Cobalamin)

B12 is remarkably safe because the body excretes what it doesn't need. There is no established upper limit for intake.

  • Risks: Extremely high blood levels are occasionally linked to increased mortality or hip fractures in some studies, but these are often markers of underlying disease (like liver or kidney issues) rather than toxicity from the vitamin itself.
  • Side Effects: High doses might cause acne or skin rashes in rare cases.
